question: Does the active work test the user's primary goal: accurate physical obstacle forecasts for independent motion and responses to the robot's actions, with learned heads allowed?
hypothesis: Task-aligned physical forecast and matched action-response measures distinguish useful prediction from representation aesthetics or latent-distance planning. Toy work is useful only where it tests a relevant failure more efficiently.

sources.sections: Sections4.3-4.4; AppendixA.3 lines321-337 and A.10 lines482-488, revisited before this scope correction
sources.consequence: Separate training-only auxiliary supervision, post-training state readout and inference-time physical heads. Linear and MLP readouts test different accessibility; a usable physical decoder is permitted.

sources.sections: Section3 future ego-motion conditioning; Section4 robot future encoder lines314-320; Section5 ADE/FDE definitions and Table5 conditional evaluation
sources.consequence: Forecast obstacle trajectories conditional on candidate ego motion and measure physical errors. A conditional forecast evaluated on one recorded future does not establish the correctness of counterfactual action effects.

sources.sections: Sections4.1-4.2, object observability and identity anchor
sources.consequence: Object masking is a proposed means of improving prediction; clean slots or latent-only inference are not project success criteria.

differences: This is a documentation and source audit, not a new model, training run, dataset, metric calculation or result reinterpretation. Existing Go2/ring evaluations include learned readouts and matched reaction tests. Current non-interacting balls cannot demonstrate reactive obstacle forecasting. No published architecture is adopted here.
contrary_evidence: Go2 already tested ridge, MLP and spatial heads; adding another head experiment without identifying a missing comparison could repeat prior work. M5's aggregate Genesis forecast improvement does not establish accurate reactions; P24's Genesis reaction experiment was not run. P26 uses recorded future ego poses and requires separate deployment and counterfactual validation.

protocol.scope: Record the user's clarified objective, audit existing head and forecast measures, update active guidance, preserve historical protocols/results and keep the in-flight O0 runtime unchanged.
protocol.verification: Check documentation links, actual head/metric code, unchanged runtime files, exact existing result-review bindings and publication; no new scientific computation.

success: Active guidance prioritizes physical forecast and action-response accuracy, accepts learned heads, retains useful toy work and explicitly identifies what balls, ring and offline Genesis can and cannot test.
stop: This record does not authorize a new experiment or bypass existing predecessor checks. Freeze data splits, head training/selection, metrics, baselines and acceptance criteria in a separate literature-gated experimental record before implementation or execution. No automatic successor solely to fill the old planning matrix.
